scenes.narration: This slide introduces a specialized EC2 placement requirement: clock precision. In the first panel, a precision-time placement group places supported instances on hardware with access to high-precision time sources. This is different from the normal goal of putting machines close together for low-latency packet exchange. Move to the second purple panel. Enhanced Amazon Time Sync capabilities depend on the actual instance family, Region and configuration; you must verify support rather than assume every EC2 instance gains the same clock accuracy. In the third panel, a clock icon branches into network latency, hardware isolation and clock accuracy. These are three independent concerns. A tightly clustered network might have low latency and still not satisfy precision timestamping requirements. Finally, the fourth panel shows monitoring. Measure synchronization accuracy against the application's tolerances, record clock drift and test your workload's time-dependent behavior. The bottom takeaway warns against treating precision-time placement as a substitute for data replication, backups or Multi-AZ recovery. Choose it when timestamps truly matter, then design reliability separately.

scenes.narration: This last observability slide makes you check where each metric originates before taking an action. Start at the top-left yellow CPU panel. EC2 publishes CPU utilization, and eligible burstable instances also expose credit balance and usage. Unlimited configurations may include surplus-credit metrics, which explain charges or sustained bursting. Move to the upper-right network panel. NetworkIn and NetworkOut report bytes, while packet metrics and instance-specific network limits help diagnose packet-rate pressure. A high throughput reading does not by itself identify packet drops or application delay. In the lower-left storage panel, local disk counters represent instance-store IO; use EBS volume metrics and supported Nitro EBS metrics for block-volume behavior. Do not mistake one storage metric for another. The lower-right guest panel is especially important: memory utilization and filesystem free space are not standard EC2 host metrics. You need a CloudWatch agent or custom instrumentation. Finally, the bottom-left cadence box distinguishes basic monitoring, generally five-minute intervals, from eligible detailed monitoring at one-minute resolution, while some metric families have their own cadence. Check source, units and sampling before changing instance size or scaling policy.
